agent_audits.analysis: Read all six production module/API surfaces (src/test.rs is test data), both manifests, comparison dispatch, UTF-8 splitting, integer-overflow fallback, GNU ordering and manifest changes. No unsafe, build script, FFI, I/O, subprocess or network. Numeric parsing is checked; string slicing occurs only after leading ASCII-digit checks, and public part access rejects out-of-range indices. Recursive comparison swaps exhausted iterators at most once. This is documented best-effort version ordering, not SemVer or a security-version-floor validator: large numeric strings become text on i32 overflow, zero/punctuation-only inputs and mixed text follow permissive semantics, and set_manifest does not reparse existing parts. Long digit sequences can take superlinear CPU because nth rescans prefixes; downstream callers must bound hostile lengths. In this desktop graph the consumer is system-deps build-time native-library discovery using trusted build metadata, not an unbounded network request parser. 30 upstream unit tests and one synthetic test covering BMP Unicode scalar variations, numeric overflow and bounds passed on pinned Rust 1.100 Windows. No cross-platform, timing or full semantic-equivalence proof is claimed.

agent_audits.analysis: Read both manifests and all three complete Rust modules. The macro parser requires unsafe type declarations, accepts only explicit Send/Sync markers and obtains CType/drop/clone/PhantomData from trusted Rust source, not runtime input. Generated owned wrappers contain NonNull pointers; unchecked construction remains inside unsafe ForeignType::from_ptr, and deref/borrow references remain tied to self. Drop frees once, optional Clone/ToOwned requires a caller-supplied cloning function returning a distinct valid owned reference; arbitrary aliasing of borrowed references still obeys the upstream ForeignType/ForeignTypeRef contract. Generated Send/Sync impls are explicit unsafe assertions by the declaring crate and must match its foreign library. The macro does not establish those external native invariants itself. proc-macro parsing uses syn/quote tokens without evaluating textual attributes, reading files, launching processes or using network. std only changes ToOwned generation. This source review covers generated production code as required by safe-to-deploy; dependencies and each downstream unsafe declaration need their own validation.
